**The real finding:** `ReviewScope` — as specified in the *frozen* interfaces.json contract itself, not something Claude A improvised — is declared `enum ReviewScope: Sendable { case deck(Deck); case allDecks }`. `Deck` is a mutable SwiftData `@Model` class, which is not `Sendable`. Under Swift 6 language mode (the default for new Xcode targets since Xcode 16), embedding a non-`Sendable` class inside a `Sendable`-conforming enum is a real, hard compile error, not a warning — and Xcode projects created today default to Swift 6 mode unless someone deliberately picks Swift 5. This has been sitting in the interface contract since tech_specs/ios_architecture_review, unnoticed across four rounds of everyone correctly building against it. It means the moment a real Xcode project exists and RecallCore lands, this specific line could be the first thing that fails to compile — not because of the RecallCore gap, but as its own separate defect. Two ways to close it, both real decisions someone needs to make deliberately rather than discover by accident: **(a)** the integrator sets the RecallApp target's Swift language mode to Swift 5 / minimal concurrency checking when creating the Xcode project (simplest, and consistent with how this project already treats SwiftData models as main-actor-affine everywhere), or **(b)** data_domain has `Deck`/`Card` adopt `@unchecked Sendable` explicitly, which is defensible here since nothing in this app ever touches these models off the main actor. I can't fix this myself — it spans the Xcode project (integrator) and possibly the model definitions (data_domain) — but it needed to be said clearly before it becomes a surprise.
